newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Bull returns to private market.
newsitem.headline: France's Bull returns to private market.

text.p: France said on Thursday it was returning computer group Cie des Machines Bull to the private market by selling 10 million shares at 22 francs ($4.17) each to NEC, Dai-Nippon Printing of Japan and Motorola of the U.S.
After a complex deal involving a 400 million franc capital increase, NEC, Motorola and state-owned France Telecom will each have 18.7 percent of Bull instead of the 17 percent they previously held.
Dai-Nippon Printing will increase its stake to 5.8 percent from 3.3 percent.
The direct stake of the government comes down to 30.5 percent, bringing the total government stake to 49.2 percent from 53 percent.
IBM saw its stake slip further to 0.7 percent from 0.8 percent. Bull staff have 3.5 percent and other investors a total 3.4 percent.

Bull, which lost 22 billion francs between 1990 and 1994, said it expected to post a net consolidated profit for 1996 after a 306 million franc profit in 1995, despite a 661 million franc negative impact on the first half results due to a restructuring of its personal computer business.
Bull merged its Zenith Data personal computer business with those of NEC and Packard Bell Electronics Inc in February.

"The sales figure for December, which makes up about 20 percent of annual sales, remains a determining factor for the result. Nevertheless the group, despite the costs related to the repositioning of the personal computer activities in the first half (with a negative impact of 661 million francs on results) expects to realise in 1996 a positive net consolidated result for the second year running," Bull said in a statement.

"For the year 1997, taking account of the non-recurrent character of the 1996 losses related to personal computers, Groupe Bull has as objective to obtain a net consolidated result significantly higher than 1996 as well as 1995," it added.

It added that the 400 million francs in capital increase included both the 10 million new shares sold by the state as well as the exercise of options acquired at 22.04 francs per share in September 1995.

The 22 franc share price of the latest share sale is twice the 1995 price which was based in the net asset per share value on December 1994 and is 1.4 times the expected net asset per share for December 31, 1996.
An extraordinary general meeting will be held on February 19 and share trading, suspended since November 26, will resume soon. ($ = 5.269 French Francs)
